title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 160
paragraphs: As for Zopyros, in Darius' judgment no Persian surpassed him in service, either of those who came after or of those who had gone before, except Cyrus alone—for no Persian has ever yet ventured to compare himself with Cyrus. Darius is said to have declared often that he would rather Zopyros were free from the injury he had done himself than have twenty Babylons added to his possessions on top of the one he already had. Moreover he gave him great honours: not only did he give him every year those gifts which the Persians count as the most honourable, but he also granted him Babylon to rule free of tribute for as long as he lived, and added many other gifts besides. The son of this Zopyros was Megabyzos, who was appointed commander in Egypt against the Athenians and their allies; and the son of this Megabyzos was Zopyros, who went over to Athens as a deserter from the Persians.
